(1) SPL7 is a key transcriptional regulator of Cu homeostasis and that (2) Cu homeostasis is essential for plant cell wall dynamics.
the Cu-dependent activities of numerous Cu-protein are involved in the properties of the plant cell wall, which is a major Cu-accumulating site in plant tissues.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the Cu trafficking in plants and its implication for the cell wall properties.
the identification and characterization of Cu-dependent activities and Cu-accumulation processes in the cell wall.
the molecular and physiological mechanisms of Cu transport and homeastasis in plants, and its implication on plant growth and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cu is a central player in plant biology, and that Cu homeostasis is tightly regulated at multiple levels.
Cu is a key player in plant development and physiology, and its homeostasis is tightly regulated at multiple levels.
Cu homeostasis in plants is tightly linked to cell wall properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a tight control on Cu transport is essential to ensure a proper Cu-dependent cell wall dynamics.
the plant cell wall is a Cu-accumulation site, and that this Cu is required for the maintenance and/or remodeling of the cell wall.
the Cu status in a plant is a dynamic process and the Cu-proteins are not just passive players, but rather actively involved in the control of Cu homeostasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cu homeostasis in plants is a highly regulated process, which is tightly linked with cell wall dynamics.
the Cu-dependent properties of the cell wall are essential in the control of plant development and adaptation to environmental stress.
the Cu-dependent properties of plant cell walls are tightly regulated and that the Cu-dependent cell wall properties are essential for plant development and survival.
